title: Large Bricks and Join-irreducible torsionfree classes

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract and introduction claim the result holds 'in the category of finitely generated modules over an artinian ring' (a very general class of rings, including non-commutative rings with no field structure). However, the Notation section restricts the entire treatment to 'Λ ... a finite-dimensional k-algebra over some field k', and all subsequent results (Prop 2.9, Lemma 3.6, Lemma 3.7, Prop 3.9) are stated and proved only for Λ-mod in this restricted sense. This is a narrower setting than 'artinian ring' as claimed in the abstract/title, so the stated generality of the main theorem is not actually established by the proofs given.

The text repeatedly cites references [1] ('we refer the reader to the survey [1]'), [2] (Lemma 3.3 as '[2, Lemma 2.3]', Proposition 3.5 as '[2, Theorem 3.6]'), and [3] (Theorem 1.1 as '[3, Theorem 1.0.5]', Corollary 2.10 as '[3], [6]'), but the provided bibliography only lists references [4] through [11], omitting entries [1]-[3] entirely. This leaves three cited sources unverifiable and inconsistent with the reference list given.

Unlike every other imported result in the paper (Theorem 1.1, Theorem 2.5, Theorem 3.2, Lemma 3.3, Proposition 3.5), which carry explicit bracketed citations to their sources, Theorem 3.1 (the bijection tors(R) ↔ Cosilt(R)) is presented as an established fact with no citation at all, despite being attributed to 'the first result' from cosilting theory. This is an inconsistency in citation practice and likely a missing citation.
